idiom_name: companion-object smart constructor returning Either/Option with a private constructor; opaque types for single values (Scala 3)
implementation_notes: A case class exposes construction through the synthesized apply and copy, so the Scala factory is a smart constructor: make the constructor private, expose a domain-named method on the companion object that validates and returns Either[E, Order] (Option when absence is enough), and use Scala 3 opaque types for single-value products at zero runtime cost. What replaces the classic factory class is the companion object, which keeps creation next to the type; a separate injected factory class remains justified when creation must load other aggregates or consult a domain service.
pitfalls: Case-class synthesis fights privacy: Scala 2 needs -Xsource:2.12 (2.11.11+) / 2.13 or a sealed abstract case class before copy and apply respect the private constructor, and forgetting it leaves the bypass open.
An Either-returning factory does nothing unless callers match on the result; an ignored Left lets invalid input travel further down the call chain.
Validating several fields with for-comprehensions on Either stops at the first failure and tends to mix error types; use an accumulating combinator when every violation must be reported.
